Reviewer: wopr pool job review-4302, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

Needs changes before merge. One blocking finding.

1. **[P2] Use native absolute paths in the folder test.** `crates/app/src/mcp/post_files.rs:172`.
   Class: platform-dependent test fixtures. The new test uses `/p/posts` and `/h` without a platform guard. On Windows, these paths have a root but no drive prefix. `Path::is_absolute()` returns false. Thus, `user_dir_for("linux", ...)` returns `None`, and the assertion on line 173 fails. The fallback assertions on lines 175 and 177 have the same problem. Use drive-qualified paths on Windows and Unix absolute paths elsewhere. Build the expected paths with `PathBuf::join`. Apply this rule to all folder cases, as `crates/app/tests/machine_edit.rs:270` already does. Keep the Windows coverage. This finding comes from source inspection; this Linux host has no Windows test target.

The command routing uses `SelectPost` and History. The six new MCP tests pass. The source uses the existing post engine limits and atomic-write helper. The process-change declaration and decision file are present.

**Local results**

Trial merge: PR head `a8890b3a1145f464d5b3639289a43920159290cb` with upstream/main `e902ee488e2d80cf84267d55898489e10400a073`. Local merge: `1b1ab8a1f1a367b83e35754e78f29de24f443a15`. `HEAD^1` is the PR head. No conflict occurred.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 176 steps passed; zero failures or stalls. Tests: 1,448 passed, 26 ignored. This includes app lib (325), MCP (62), MCP documentation drift (9), example catalog (44 passed, 4 ignored), and example catalog edge work (1).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: all six steps passed; all 11 light tests passed. No full heavy lane ran.
- An earlier quick run was void because my Python test run created untracked cache files. I removed those generated files. The complete quick rerun above passed on a clean tree.

**Extra suites run**

`python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: 104 tests, three failures and five errors. The same command on bare upstream/main has the same results. The failures concern two rotary icon copies and the missing `manualToolChange` reference row. The errors concern the missing `zola` executable. These results add no blocker for this PR. I did not identify a tracking issue for them.

No fixture or importer code changed. No UI code changed. The additional importer suites and UI screenshots do not apply.

**Mutations and goldens**

No source mutations ran. This PR adds an MCP surface over existing post services. It changes no post script, output algorithm, collision check, stock simulation, geometry algorithm, or recorded program. No goldens moved.

I read the complete diff and the issue thread. There was no earlier review to resolve. The head and ownership records were checked again before this comment. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset on this host; `review-4302` is this review session's identifier.

The review state is `needs-rework`. Per the maintainer's explicit override, I left the labels, title, and draft state unchanged. I retained `.claude/worktrees/review-4302` and its branch. I made no code change or push.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

The review fix for the review on a8890b3a1 is pushed. The new head is 9127279b5. It is one commit (NEW CODE, test code only).

Finding 1 (native absolute paths in the folder test) is fixed in `crates/app/src/mcp/post_files.rs`:

- `the_folder_follows_the_override_then_the_platform_data_dir` uses drive-qualified paths on Windows (`C:\p\posts`, `C:\h`) and Unix absolute paths on other systems.
- The expected folders are built with `PathBuf::join`, as `crates/app/tests/machine_edit.rs` does.
- The test now also covers `XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux and `APPDATA` on Windows. The case "Windows with only `HOME`" stays and gives `None`.
- `a_file_name_must_be_plain` uses a native absolute folder and `Path::join` for the expected file.
- The environment helper owns its pairs, so the test needs no `'static` lists.

I did not find other non-native absolute paths in the PR's tests. `requires_approval("preview_post", {"path": "/x.cps"})` only checks that a `path` key is present, so it is the same on each platform.

Readings on 9127279b5:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib post_files`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 176 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 41.8 min.
- No Windows target was built. The Windows branch of the test is checked by reading only.

Ready for a re-check.

Reviewer: wopr pool job review-4302-r2, Claude Opus 5.5, mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

Re-review of head `9127279b5`. The earlier finding is fixed. The PR now conflicts with upstream/main. The label is `conflicts`.

**Earlier finding (review on `a8890b3a1`)**

1. **[P2] Native absolute paths in the folder test** (`crates/app/src/mcp/post_files.rs`): **fixed** in `9127279b5`.
   - `the_folder_follows_the_override_then_the_platform_data_dir` uses `C:\...` paths on Windows and `/...` paths on other systems.
   - The expected folders are built with `PathBuf::join`.
   - The test now also covers `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `APPDATA`, the plain `HOME` Linux case, and "no home gives `None`". Each case agrees with `user_dir_for` (lines 26-37).
   - `a_file_name_must_be_plain` uses a native absolute folder and `Path::join`.
   - The fix commit changes test code only. I read the Windows branch; this host has no Windows target.

**Merge state (blocker for merge, not for the code)**

The trial merge of the PR head with upstream/main `4d891498e7270eabba1b82809d08228b465c0aec` stops with two conflicts:

1. `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`, the `GateKind::FileWrite` arm of `requires_approval`. Main added `save_library_component` and `delete_library_component`. This PR added `save_post_script`. Keep the four names in the one arm. The `select_post` row of the `LimitEdit` arm merges cleanly.
2. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`, the tool count line (128 on the PR, 132 on main). Do not edit this file by hand. After the merge, write it again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference > docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`. Then run `mcp_doc_drift`.

The two conflicts are "both sides added lines". No safety rule is in them. Use a merge of main (no rebase, no force-push), as the `resolve-conflicts` skill tells. Then run the `mcp` suite, `mcp_doc_drift` and the `camcraft-app` lib tests on the merged tree, and comment "ready for a re-check".

**Local results (PR head `9127279b5`, not merged)**

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib post_files`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The quick gate did not run: the merged tree does not exist until the conflicts are resolved. The earlier review ran the quick gate on `a8890b3a1` (176 steps, 0 failed). The fix commit changes only the two unit tests above.

**Extra suites run**

None. The diff changes no `testdata/` file and no importer code.

**Safety tier**

Not a safety-tier review. The PR adds MCP tools over the existing post engine. It changes no post script, no posted output, no gouge or collision check, no stock simulation and no geometry. No goldens moved. No mutations ran.

**UI**

No `crates/ui` change. Screenshots do not apply.

**Process**

The PR changes `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The body has `Process change: yes` and does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. This is correct.

No new finding. When the conflicts are resolved and the gate is green on the merged head, the review needs only a delta check of the merge (class DELTA, the two hunks above).

The PR stays a draft. The author flags it ready. A maintainer approves and merges an outside PR by hand.
